party_context.hired_counsel_directive:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
HIRED COUNSEL IDENTITY — READ BEFORE EVALUATING ANY CLAUSE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

You have been retained as legal counsel to advise:

  CLIENT:        Columbia Capital Management, LLC
  CONTRACT TERM: "Consultant"  ← this is the SAME legal entity
  ROLE:          Independent contractor engaged to provide professional services to the City as described in the Scope of Services.

  COUNTERPARTY:  City of Westwood, Kansas
  CONTRACT TERM: "City"
  ROLE:          Municipal corporation engaging the Consultant to perform professional services on its behalf.

  TRANSACTION:   Professional Services Agreement whereby the City of Westwood, Kansas engages Columbia Capital Management, LLC as an independent contractor to provide defined professional services.

  Key client assets to protect:
    • Right to compensation for professional services rendered under the agreed Scope of Services
    • Independent contractor status, preserving autonomy over means and methods of service delivery

  Key client burdens to limit:
    • Liability exposure for errors, omissions, or professional negligence in the performance of services
    • Scope creep obligations beyond the defined Exhibit A Scope of Services without additional compensation

IDENTITY RULE (ABSOLUTE — NO EXCEPTIONS)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
"Columbia Capital Management, LLC" and "Consultant" are THE SAME ENTITY.
They are not two different parties. Never draft language that
imposes obligations of "Consultant" ON "Columbia Capital Management, LLC"
or vice versa. Never invent a third party label not defined in
the agreement (e.g. do not use "Provider" unless the agreement
defines it as such).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
DIRECTIONAL ANALYSIS RULES (APPLY TO EVERY CLAUSE)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Classify every contractual provision using this four-rule test:

  RULE 1 — DUTY ON CLIENT = BURDEN
    A clause that imposes an obligation, liability, restriction,
    or deadline on "Consultant" creates a burden on
    your client. Evaluate whether the burden is excessive,
    unqualified, or disproportionate. Flag only genuine
    commercial or legal overreach — not routine contractual duties.

  RULE 2 — RIGHT FOR CLIENT = ASSET (DO NOT FLAG)
    A clause that grants a right, power, remedy, or discretion
    TO "Consultant" is an asset for your client.
    Do NOT characterise an asset as a risk. Do NOT recommend
    removing or softening a clause that benefits your client.

  RULE 3 — DUTY ON COUNTERPARTY = CLIENT PROTECTION (DO NOT FLAG)
    A clause that imposes an obligation, liability, or restriction
    on "City" protects your client.
    Do NOT characterise this as a risk or imbalance.

  RULE 4 — FAVOURABLE ASYMMETRY = CLIENT WIN (DO NOT FLAG)
    If a clause is one-sided in favour of "Consultant",
    that asymmetry is a commercial benefit for your client.
    Do NOT flag one-sided client-favourable terms as defects.
    Only flag one-sided counterparty-favourable terms.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
DRAFTING CONSTRAINT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
When drafting a suggested fix:
• Address only the specific legal deficiency identified.
• Use ONLY defined terms from the agreement (never synonyms).
• "Consultant" refers to your client — never impose
  burdens on this entity in the fix unless necessary to cure an
  identified deficiency that the client itself needs addressed.
• Do not turn a targeted fix into an omnibus rewrite of the clause.

PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

THIS PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (“Agreement”) is entered into this    day of May, 2024, by and between the City of Westwood, Kansas, a municipal corporation (“City,”) and Columbia Capital Management, LLC, a Missouri limited liability company having its principle place of business in Merriam, Kansas (“Consultant”).

WHEREAS, the City needs professional assistance to perform the services outlined in the Scope of Services described in Exhibit A; and

WHEREAS, the Consultant represents that it has sufficient experience and qualified personnel to perform the professional services herein described on behalf of the City; and

WHEREAS, The City has determined, based upon information provided by the Consultant, that Consultant is qualified to provide the professional services described herein.

WHEREAS, the City and Consultant desire to enter into this Agreement to set forth the specific terms and conditions of their relationship.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, the parties agree as follows:

explanation_call.reason: As currently drafted, the clause records Columbia Capital Management's unconditional acceptance of the engagement but imposes no express corresponding obligation on the City — most critically, no commitment to compensate Consultant for the services it has agreed to perform. While payment terms are likely addressed elsewhere in the Agreement, anchoring the City's reciprocal compensation obligation at the point of engagement provides Columbia Capital Management with a cleaner contractual basis should a payment dispute arise. Without it, the engagement clause reads as a one-way commitment by the Consultant only.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
SECTION 2. Services.

Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

Subcontracting Services. Consultant may not, without first obtaining the City’s written consent, subcontract any of the Contract Services. Notwithstanding the City’s consent to any subcontracting, Consultant shall remain fully responsible for all obligations under this Agreement.

Time of Performance. The Consultant agrees to complete the Contract Services within the times listed in Exhibit A, Scope of Service. In absence of written directions to the contrary, receipt of the executed Agreement shall be the Consultant’s Notice to Proceed. At the City’s discretion, an extension of time may be granted to the  Consultant for delays determined by the City as unavoidable. Consultant may request an extension of time stating the reasons for such a request. The term of this Agreement may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties beyond the time periods outlined in Exhibit A for the purpose of the Consultant providing any additional services, as outlined in Exhibit A, as may be requested by City and agreed to by Consultant. The Parties agree that time for performance of the Contract Services is of the essence and that the Consultant’s failure to meet the contractual times for performance shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement.

Qualified Personnel. Consultant shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Contract Services. If directed by the City, the Consultant shall remove any person the Consultant employs in connection with the work.

Performance. In performing the Contract Services, Consultant agrees to take all steps necessary for the full and effective performance of those tasks.

Assistance from City. To assist Consultant in performing the Contract Services, the City will perform the duties outlined in Exhibit A, if any, in a timely manner so as not to unreasonably delay the Consultant’s services.

explanation_call.reason: Section 3 as drafted does nothing more than redirect to Exhibit A, leaving Columbia Capital Management entirely unprotected on the core mechanics of payment: there is no invoicing procedure, no payment deadline binding the City, no fixed-fee confirmation, no late-payment remedy, and no expense reimbursement framework. In practice, the City could delay payment indefinitely, contest invoices without constraint, and refuse expense reimbursement, and Columbia Capital Management would have no express contractual basis to enforce timely payment or accrue interest on overdue amounts. explanation_call.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement. The Consultant shall submit invoices to the City on a monthly basis, and the City shall remit payment of all undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days following receipt of each invoice. Fees are fixed as set forth in Exhibit A and shall not be modified except by written amendment executed by both parties. Reimbursable expenses, if any, shall be as specified in Exhibit A. If the City disputes any portion of an invoice, the City shall notify the Consultant in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, identifying the disputed amount and the basis for the dispute; undisputed amounts shall be paid by the original due date. Any invoice amount remaining unpaid after thirty (30) days shall accrue interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less, until paid in full.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
SECTION 7. Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules.

Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.

Solicitations. In all solicitations or advertisements for employees, Consultant shall include the phrase “equal opportunity employer” or a similar phrase approved by the Kansas Human Rights Commission (Commission).

Non-Compliance. Consultant shall be deemed to have breached this Agreement and it may be cancelled, terminated, or suspended in whole or in part by the City, if the Consultant:

fails to comply with the reporting requirements of K.S.A. 44-1031 or K.S.A. 44-1116, and amendments thereto; or

is found guilty of the Kansas Act Against Discrimination or the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act under a decision or order of the Commission that has become final.

Flow Through Requirements. Consultant shall include the provisions of Section 7(a)-(c) in every subcontract so that such provisions will be binding upon such subcontractor for work related to the City.

Exempt Contractors. The provisions of this Section 7(a)-(d) are recommended but not enforceable against Consultant if:

Consultant employs fewer than four employees at all times during the term of this Agreement; or

All of Consultant’s contracts with the City cumulatively total $5,000 or less during the fiscal year of the City pursuant to K.S.A. 44-1030(c).

ADA Compliance. Consultant agrees to comply with the American with Disabilities Act of 1990 (“ADA”), codified as amended at 42 U.S.C. § 12101 et seq., as well as all other federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, rules, and regulations applicable to this project and to furnish any and all certification that may be required by federal, state, or local governmental agencies in connection therewith.

Code Compliance. Consultant agrees to comply with Chapter 35, Article III of the Westwood Code, which prohibits discrimination in employment, housing, and public accommodations on the basis of an individual’s sexual orientation or gender identity.

More significantly for Columbia Capital Management, the clause is entirely silent on the relationship between the insurance requirements and the Consultant's underlying contractual liability: without an express non-expansion clause, the City could argue that the prescribed coverage amounts constitute a floor establishing the minimum scope of the Consultant's exposure, inadvertently broadening Columbia Capital Management's financial liability beyond any cap or limitation provided elsewhere in the Agreement. Adding a brief non-expansion sentence directly protects Columbia Capital Management from that construction while a narrow tail-coverage qualifier, limited to claims-made policies only, resolves the duration gap without imposing a blanket post-termination obligation on occurrence-based programs.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, and for a period of one (1) year following expiration or termination of this Agreement solely with respect to any coverage maintained on a claims-made basis pursuant to written agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The procurement and maintenance of insurance as required herein shall not be construed to expand, limit, or otherwise modify the Consultant's liability beyond the terms expressly set forth in this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. SECTION 8. Insurance.

General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

Notice of Claim. Consultant, upon receiving notice of any claim in connection with this Agreement, shall promptly notify the City, providing full details thereof, including an estimate of the amount of loss or liability.

Reduction of Policy Limits. Consultant shall monitor and promptly notify the City of any reduction in limits of protection afforded under any policy listed in the Certificate (or otherwise required by this Agreement) if the Consultant’s limits of protection have been impaired or reduced to such extent that the limits fall below the minimum amounts required hereunder. In that event, Consultant shall promptly reinstate the original limits of liability required hereunder and shall furnish evidence thereof to the City.

Industry Ratings. Consultant agrees that its insurance carrier must:

a. Be licensed to do business in the State of Kansas;

b. Carry a Best’s policyholder rating of “A-” or better and;

c. Carry at least a Class VIII financial rating; OR

Be acceptable to the City.

Insurance Required. Consultant agrees to secure and maintain the following insurance:

Commercial General Liability. Consultant shall maintain General Liability coverage including Premises-Operations Liability, Independent Contractors Liability, Products and Completed Operations, and Broad Form Property Damage within these minimum limits:

Bodily Injury & Property Damage	$1,000,000 combined single limit per occurrence: $2,000,000 annual aggregate

Fire Damage Liability	$50,000

Medical Payments	$5,000

The property damage liability coverage shall contain no exclusion relative to blasting, explosion, collapse of buildings, or damages to underground property.

Comprehensive Automobile Liability. Consultant shall maintain Automobile Liability coverage including coverage for Owned, Hired and Non-owned Auto Liability providing for all injuries to members of the public and damage to property of others arising from the use of motor vehicles on and off the Work site with these minimum limits:

Bodily Injury & Property Damage	$1,000,000 combined single limit per occurrence

Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability. Consultant shall maintain Workers’ Compensation coverage for all claims made under applicable state workers’ compensation laws. Consultant shall also maintain Employer’s Liability coverage for claims made for injury, disease, or death of an employee that, for any reason, may not fall within the provisions of a workers’ compensation law. The following minimum limits shall apply:

Workers’ Compensation	Statutory Limits

Employers’ Liability	$500,000 each accident; $500,000 disease – policy limit; $500,000 disease – each employee

Professional Liability Insurance. Consultant shall maintain Professional Liability Insurance in an amount of no less than $1,000,000.

Subcontractor’s Insurance. If a part of this Agreement is to be sublet, the Consultant shall either:

Cover all subcontractors under its insurance policies; or

Require each subcontractor not so covered to secure insurance that will protect subcontractor against all applicable hazards or risks of loss as and in the minimum amounts designated.

Whichever option is chosen, Consultant shall indemnify and hold harmless the City as to any and all damages, claims, or losses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the acts or omissions of its subcontractors.

Let me analyze this indemnification clause carefully from the perspective of Columbia Capital Management (the "Consultant") as the represented client.

The clause reads: "Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision."
Checking IND-01, the triggers are clearly spelled out — claims from performance of services caused by negligent or intentional acts, errors, or omissions — so this looks satisfied. For IND-02, the direction is one-sided: only Consultant indemnifies City, with no reciprocal obligation flowing back.

Moving to IND-03, the covered losses list damages, losses, liabilities, costs, expenses, and attorneys' fees — more than two kinds named, so this is met. Now I'm checking IND-04 on mutuality, and since it's one-sided, I need to see whether it's at least limited to matters within Consultant's control, which seems tied to the "caused by" language.

From the Consultant's side, the "in whole or in part" phrasing is troubling — it means Consultant could be fully liable even if the City shares most of the fault, since the trigger only requires that Consultant's negligence be part of the cause. Weighing this against the criterion, I'd call it "Partly met" since it's one-sided and the "in whole or in part" wording stretches liability beyond matters strictly within Consultant's control.

Looking next at claim-handling mechanics — notice, defense control, and cooperation — the clause only requires the Consultant to give the City immediate written notice of any claim; it says nothing about who controls the defense or any mutual cooperation duty, and nothing about the City notifying Consultant. With only one of the three elements present, this is also "Partly met."

explanation_thinking_by_para.DD546C92:
Let me analyze the issues and draft a surgical fix for Columbia Capital Management (Consultant).

Key issues to address:
1. Indemnity is one-sided (only Consultant indemnifies City) - needs reciprocal City indemnity or at minimum fault-based limitation
2. Notice provision says "immediate" written notice - this is an obligation on Consultant (burden on client), should be reasonable/prompt notice period
3. No cap interaction - the "without in any way limiting" language is dangerous as it could override any liability cap
4. No duty on City to mitigate/limit its losses
5. No defense control rights for Consultant - no right to control defense, approve settlements
6. Also need claims handling provisions giving Consultant the right to control defense and approve settlements before finalizing the fix.

I'm also noting City should bear a duty to mitigate damages, and I need to keep the revised clause within about 20% of the original's 170-word length, so roughly 136-204 words total. I'm drafting the indemnification section now, making it mutual and subjecting it to the Agreement's liability caps, while swapping "immediate" notice for "prompt" notice.

I'm flagging that the "without in any way limiting" phrasing is risky since it suggests the indemnity escapes any liability caps elsewhere in the agreement—a high-risk point for Consultant. I'm revising the indemnification clause to be mutual and subject to any liability limitations in the Agreement, triggered when a negligent or intentional act causes the claim.

I'm adding requirements for prompt written notice, reasonable control of defense/settlement, and a mitigation duty, keeping the word count close to the original while addressing all four flagged issues—mutuality, cap interaction, notice standard, and mitigation. This version looks solid, so I'm finalizing the rationale.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 9 imposes a unilateral indemnification obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management (Consultant) with no reciprocal protection for acts or omissions of the City, exposing Consultant to open-ended liability for losses that may be caused substantially by the City's own conduct. The "Without in any way limiting" prefatory language is particularly dangerous because it expressly overrides any liability cap or limitation of liability provision that may exist elsewhere in the Agreement, rendering Consultant's financial exposure potentially uncapped. The notice obligation requiring "immediate" written notice of any claim imposes an unrealistically strict trigger that could be used by the City to defeat Consultant's indemnity rights if notification is delayed even briefly, and the clause contains no mechanism for Consultant to control the defense or approve settlements, nor does it require the City to take reasonable steps to mitigate its losses. These deficiencies together create material financial and operational risk for Columbia Capital Management that must be corrected.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Subject to any limitation of liability provisions set forth in this Agreement, each party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other party and its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the Indemnifying Party's performance of its obligations under this Agreement, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Indemnifying Party, its subcontractors, or anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them. The indemnified party shall: (i) give the Indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim, suit, or demand subject to this provision; (ii) grant the Indemnifying Party reasonable control of the defense and settlement of such claim, provided that the Indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim that imposes liability or obligation on the indemnified party without the indemnified party's prior written consent; and (iii) take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its losses.

Section 12. Representations. The Consultant certifies that:

The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.

The Consultant has not knowingly influenced and promises that it will not knowingly influence a City employee or former City employee to breach any ethical standard.

The Consultant has not violated, is not violating, and promises that it will not violate the City’s policy of prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks.

The Consultant represents that it has not retained and will not retain a person to solicit or secure a City contract upon an agreement or understanding for a commission, percentage, brokerage, or contingent fee, except for retention of bona fide employees or bona fide established commercial selling agencies for the purpose of securing business.

The Consultant is currently unaware of any conflict of interest with any party affected by this Agreement. Consultant agrees that if any conflict of interest should arise in the future, it will give notice to the City immediately.

Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.

Consultant warrants that the individuals who have signed this Agreement have the legal power, right, and authority to make this Agreement and to bind the Consultant.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 17 addresses only the City's payment obligations under the Kansas Cash-Basis Law but imposes no mutual compliance framework, no obligation on the City to notify Columbia Capital Management of a compliance breach affecting the Agreement, and no mechanism to adjust Consultant's compensation if a change in applicable law materially increases the cost of performance. suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. Each party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and shall promptly notify the other party in writing if it becomes aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects this Agreement. If any change in applicable law materially increases the cost or burden of Consultant's performance, the parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable adjustment to the fees payable under this Agreement. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

The issue is that "any legal actions arising out of this Agreement" is ambiguous - it's unclear whether it covers only contract claims or also tort claims, equitable claims, statutory claims, etc. The phrase "legal actions" could be read differently by two reasonable lawyers - some might read it narrowly as only actions based on the contract itself, while others might read it broadly to include all disputes related to the parties' relationship.

For Columbia Capital Management (Consultant), the ambiguity cuts both ways, but the concern is that a court might interpret "arising out of this Agreement" narrowly, potentially allowing the City to bring certain related claims (e.g., tort claims, statutory claims) in a different venue that could be less convenient or favorable for the Consultant. Alternatively, the clause might be read to exclude equitable relief (like injunctions), which could be important to Columbia Capital Management.
"Legal actions" also specifically risks excluding equitable proceedings like injunctions or specific performance, and "arising out of" is narrower than "relating to," potentially missing connected claims. A broad, clear venue clause benefits Columbia Capital Management by providing certainty, so I'd recommend revising the language to "actions or proceedings arising out of or relating to this Agreement" to cover both legal and equitable matters — overall this is a low-risk issue.

The issue identified is that the phrase "such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is ambiguous - it's unclear what standard governs the reformation, who decides how the provision is reformed, and what the reformed provision would actually say. Two reasonable lawyers could read this differently: one might read it as the provision self-executing (automatically reforming without court involvement), another might read it as requiring judicial reformation. The ambiguity lies in "automatically" - there's no mechanism specified for how this reformation occurs.

From Columbia Capital Management's (Consultant's) perspective, this ambiguity is risky because a court could interpret the reformation in a way that is unfavorable to Consultant. 

The "automatically" language leaves it unclear whether the City could unilaterally decide what the reformed provision says, or whether it could be construed to maximize Consultant's obligations - so I want to fix this by specifying that reformation should occur only to the minimum extent necessary to make the provision valid, and that it should be done by the parties or a court rather than happening "automatically" with no clear actor or standard.

Because the reformation occurs "automatically" rather than through judicial or mutual intervention, a counterparty or court could interpret this language to maximize the scope of a reformulated obligation in a way unfavorable to Columbia Capital Management, rather than limiting reformation to the narrowest adjustment necessary to achieve validity. Anchoring the reformation standard to the minimum extent necessary to make the provision valid and enforceable removes that interpretive uncertainty and protects Columbia Capital Management from an expansive judicial or unilateral rewrite of any challenged provision.

3. The indemnification obligation surviving without a time limit creates uncapped/indefinite financial exposure for Columbia Capital Management.
4. There's no mirrored survival of City's own obligations, and the catch-all phrase is ambiguous on top of that.

My fixes should make the clause mutual by including City's payment obligations, narrow or replace the vague catch-all with enumerated terms applying equally to both parties, and cap indemnification survival to a defined period or the statute of limitations. I'm restructuring Section 27 into separate subsections: one capping Consultant's indemnification survival at two years, and another making City's payment obligations survive termination as well, then I still need to resolve how to handle the remaining catch-all language.

I'm now reconsidering the Insurance section specifically—maintaining insurance post-termination is an odd and burdensome requirement when there's no ongoing engagement, so I'm leaning toward dropping or qualifying that survival clause rather than including it broadly.

Finalizing the clause: I'll cap Indemnification survival at two years, add explicit survival of City's obligation to pay accrued unpaid amounts, tighten the catch-all to only cover terms that "by their express terms" survive, and make that catch-all apply equally to both parties. suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the survivorship clause imposes post-termination burdens exclusively on Columbia Capital Management—requiring indefinite maintenance of Insurance and Indemnification obligations—while imposing no corresponding post-termination obligations on City, most critically the obligation to pay any fees accrued and outstanding at termination. The open-ended catch-all, "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination," is sufficiently vague that City could invoke it to extend any provision of the Agreement against Columbia Capital Management after the engagement ends, creating indeterminate and potentially uncapped financial exposure. The absence of a durational limit on the surviving Indemnification obligation means Columbia Capital Management could face post-termination claims arising from stale allegations with no temporal ceiling. Removing the Insurance survival (which imposes an ongoing, unworkable maintenance burden post-engagement), capping Indemnification survival, adding City's payment survival obligation, and anchoring the catch-all to both parties equally and to express terms only resolves all four identified deficiencies.

The phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is materially ambiguous: two reasonable counsel could disagree on its scope, and a court could interpret it to encompass any statute, regulation, or ordinance arguably touching investment management, exposing Columbia Capital Management to unlimited compliance liability for legal requirements it may not have had reason to anticipate at execution. explanation_call.reason: The "in addition to, but not in lieu of" construction expressly layers a contractual fiduciary standard on top of all applicable statutory standards, creating a separate and potentially broader basis for liability against Columbia Capital Management beyond what governing law already imposes — an additive exposure that is commercially unjustified and entirely one-sided. The undefined phrase "enterprise of like character and with like aims" introduces genuine interpretive ambiguity: without anchoring that benchmark to a public investment management context, the City could argue in a dispute that the applicable comparator enterprise carries a more demanding standard than the mandate Columbia Capital Management actually undertook. Additionally, the clause contains no limitation tethering the fiduciary duty to the scope of Columbia Capital Management's actual discretionary authority under the Agreement, which risks extending fiduciary exposure to decisions or outcomes outside the Consultant's control. Revising the clause to align the contractual standard with applicable law, anchoring the prudent-person benchmark to a public investment management mandate, and scoping the duty to the Consultant's discretionary authority eliminates these compounding risks.

Let me analyze the clause text carefully against each criterion from Columbia Capital Management's (the Consultant's) perspective.

The clause states:
1. Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to assets it manages
2. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform duties with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence of a "prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters" in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.

Let me evaluate each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations?**
This clause imposes obligations exclusively on the Consultant (Columbia Capital Management). The City has no reciprocal fiduciary or similar obligation. 

The standard applies "in addition to, but not in lieu of" any applicable fiduciary standards under federal or state law, which stacks contractual and statutory obligations entirely onto the Consultant with nothing reciprocal from the City — this is clearly one-sided and disadvantages Columbia Capital Management by compounding its exposure beyond baseline legal requirements. I'm now weighing whether this truly counts as one-sided under GEN-01's intended scope.

For GEN-02, there's no time standard language at all in this clause, so there's nothing vague to flag — but since the criterion says it always applies, I need to confirm "not applicable" is the right conclusion when no timing obligations exist whatsoever.

Moving to GEN-03, this clause has no financial amounts, caps, or payment terms, so that criterion is also not applicable here.

For GEN-04, I'm checking whether terms like "fiduciary," "prudent person," and "assets it manages" are adequately defined — the prudent person standard is a recognized legal concept, but phrases like "enterprise of like character and with like aims" feel vague since it's unclear what comparison point is intended.

I'm recognizing that this phrase actually mirrors ERISA § 404(a)(1)(B) language, so despite surface ambiguity, it's a well-established legal formulation — I'll mark GEN-04 as "Met" since most terms carry plain legal meaning.

Now for GEN-05, I'm weighing whether the fiduciary standard here creates unlimited liability exposure, since the clause doesn't include any cap and explicitly layers on top of other applicable fiduciary standards — without visibility into a separate limitation-of-liability clause, this provision alone appears to expose the Consultant to uncapped fiduciary liability.

For GEN-08, I'm noting this clause imposes obligations solely on the Consultant with no reciprocal right stated within the clause itself, though the broader PSA likely provides compensation elsewhere — I need to decide whether to judge this clause in isolation or in context of the full agreement.

Given Rule 3's guidance to flag imbalances that disadvantage the represented client, I'll lean toward "Partly met" for GEN-08 since the extra duties favor the City. For GEN-09, I'm weighing whether "prudent person" and "like character and aims" language, while legally established, creates ambiguity in this municipal context — possibly "Partly met" rather than fully "Met."

Now checking GEN-10: the triggering condition is clear, tied to the Consultant managing assets under the Agreement, so that's "Met." I'm going through the remaining checks systematically — one-sidedness of obligations, no time-sensitive terms, no financial figures, the undefined "like enterprise" standard, unlimited fiduciary exposure without caps, no placeholders, and no contradictions so far.

explanation_thinking_by_para.BF539E01:
Let me analyze the issues identified with this Fiduciary clause from the perspective of Columbia Capital Management (the Consultant).

Key issues:
1. The clause imposes fiduciary duties "in addition to, but not in lieu of" all applicable federal or state law fiduciary standards - this is additive and potentially creates exposure beyond statutory standards, which is one-sided against the Consultant.
2. "a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims" - the phrase "enterprise of like character and with like aims" is undefined and ambiguous.
3. Unlimited/uncapped financial liability - fiduciary duty without limitation creates potentially unlimited exposure for the Consultant.
4. All obligations flow one-way from Consultant to City with no reciprocal duties.

For fixes, I want to make the standard coextensive with, rather than additive to, applicable statutory fiduciary standards, so the Consultant isn't stacked with layered liability. I also need to tighten the undefined "enterprise of like character" language to reduce ambiguity.

I'll qualify the fiduciary duty so it applies only within the scope of the Consultant's discretionary authority under the Agreement and subject to the City's investment guidelines. I'm drafting replacement language that swaps "In addition to, but not in lieu of" for "Consistent with," limits the fiduciary scope to the Consultant's delegated authority, and clarifies the "like character and aims" phrase by referencing a comparable public investment management mandate.

I'm checking the word count against the original to confirm the revision stays within range, then drafting the rationale: the original clause stacks fiduciary obligations on top of statutory standards with no reciprocal duty from the City, and the undefined "enterprise of like character" language creates ambiguity.

The undefined phrase "enterprise of like character and with like aims" introduces genuine interpretive ambiguity: without anchoring that benchmark to a public investment management context, the City could argue in a dispute that the applicable comparator enterprise carries a more demanding standard than the mandate Columbia Capital Management actually undertook. Additionally, the clause contains no limitation tethering the fiduciary duty to the scope of Columbia Capital Management's actual discretionary authority under the Agreement, which risks extending fiduciary exposure to decisions or outcomes outside the Consultant's control. clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Investment Management Services.

Consultant’s scope of services shall include:

Providing recommendations to the City regarding updating, developing and maintaining an investment policy for the City, consistent with various Kansas statutes pertaining to deposits, investments and collateral management. Philosophically, the City’s investments will be evaluated for safety, liquidity and yield, in that order, with the recognition that ensuring adequate liquidity is also often the best way to preserve principal (safety).

Implementing an investment strategy that allocates the City’s pooled cash into multiple subportfolios with the investments in each subportfolio targeted to the unique needs for and statutory constraints on those subportfolios. Subordinate to the core investment goals of preserving principal and providing adequate liquidity, Consultant shall seek to maximize income from the portfolio that the City can use to support its operations.

Complying with Kansas the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675 et seq. providing local banks with a “first look” at the City’s investment opportunities where required.

Monitoring and marking-to-market the collateral posted by the City’s bank depositories on a weekly basis to ensure compliance with state law and City policy.

Selecting investment securities for the City’s portfolio, consistent with state law and the City’s investment policy.

Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.

Working with the city attorney to draft an ordinance designating certain of the City’s funds as multi-year capital funds.

Providing the City with general market information, ad hoc reporting and other routine requests related to investment management.

Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Columbia Capital Management to two material risks. First, the City retains an unfettered right to change investment policy objectives and guidelines "from time to time" with no advance notice requirement or transition period, meaning Columbia Capital Management could be held in breach for executing trades under existing guidelines before it has any reasonable opportunity to implement newly issued guidelines. Second, the obligation to use investment strategies that "ensure" that "total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances" creates what amounts to an absolute warranty of best-priced execution on every trade — a standard that no professional investment manager can guarantee in volatile or illiquid markets and that would expose Columbia Capital Management to uncapped liability for any transaction in which a better price was theoretically available. These two provisions together — an uncontrolled unilateral power for the City to revise guidelines without notice, and an absolute transactional performance warranty — impose commercially unjustifiable obligations on Columbia Capital Management with no corresponding protection.

explanation_call.reason: The clause as drafted contains no contractual obligation to disclose an actual or potential conflict of interest, leaving the City free to assert open-ended fiduciary or common-law claims against Columbia Capital Management if any undisclosed conflict later materializes, with no contractual benchmark defining what disclosure was required or when. That gap is commercially dangerous for Columbia Capital Management precisely because it has no safe harbor: compliance with an undefined duty is impossible to demonstrate after the fact. By adding a narrowly framed disclosure obligation—limited to known, material conflicts that directly affect the City's Accounts—Columbia Capital Management establishes a clear, objective compliance standard that cabins both its duty and the City's ability to allege concealment. The consequence language is drafted as a mutual good-faith determination, preserving Columbia Capital Management's operational flexibility rather than creating a unilateral City right to suspend or terminate.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. Consultant shall promptly notify the City in writing of any known, material conflict of interest that directly affects the management of the City's Accounts, and upon such disclosure the parties shall in good faith determine an appropriate course of action with respect to the affected investment activity. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

Let me analyze this clause carefully against each criterion from Columbia Capital Management's (Consultant's) perspective.

The clause text is:
"Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City."

Let me evaluate each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations**
The clause has an asymmetry - the City can amend Schedule X "at any time" with just notice to the Consultant. 

This gives the City unilateral power to change authorized representatives and their authority without Consultant's consent, which is somewhat one-sided, though fairly standard for a government client managing its own personnel designations. The Consultant's corresponding benefit is only the right to use aggregate, non-identifying performance data - there's no reciprocal right for Consultant to amend terms unilaterally.

I'd lean toward marking this "Partly met" given the one-sided but commercially reasonable amendment right. Turning to the vague time standards issue, there's no defined notice period for when the City must inform Consultant of changes to Schedule X - the clause just says "with notice provided" without specifying timing, which is itself a vague standard worth flagging.

On financial amounts, this clause doesn't reference any specific figures, so that's not applicable here. For undefined terms, "Accounts" and "Schedule X" appear to be capitalized defined terms addressed elsewhere, while "aggregate performance data" and "authorities" carry plain commercial meaning even without explicit definitions.

Liability isn't addressed in this clause either, so that's also not applicable. The naming of "Schedule X" strikes me as odd though - schedules are typically labeled with letters or numbers, so "X" raises the possibility it's an unfilled placeholder rather than a genuine reference, even though the clause treats it as attached and incorporated.

Turning to internal contradictions, I don't see any within this clause itself, though I can't assess cross-document consistency without the full agreement. More importantly, I'm noticing an imbalance: the City can unilaterally amend Schedule X with mere notice, while the Consultant has no right to approve, object, or negotiate those changes - this is a one-sided right that could let the City alter authority designations without any Consultant input.

I also see ambiguity worth flagging - "notice provided to Consultant" doesn't specify advance versus concurrent timing, and "aggregate data that does not identify the City" is unclear on what level of identifiability is meant. The triggers for these provisions are otherwise fairly clear, tied to Schedule X's existence and the "at any time" amendment language, so I'm working through how to score each item: likely "Partly met" for the unpaired rights and ambiguity issues, "Met" for triggers and internal consistency.

Looking more closely at "Schedule X," that naming is atypical for a real contract - schedules are usually lettered or numbered sequentially, so "X" reads like an unfilled placeholder rather than the 24th schedule in sequence. I'll mark that as "Not met" since the more plausible explanation is a drafting placeholder rather than an actual extensive schedule list.

Each invoice is due and payable within thirty (30) days following receipt. Any undisputed portion of an invoice shall remain due and payable by that date notwithstanding any good-faith dispute raised by City with respect to the remaining balance. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, excluding any pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. Consultant shall promptly notify the City in writing of any known, material conflict of interest that directly affects the management of the City's Accounts, and upon such disclosure the parties shall in good faith determine an appropriate course of action with respect to the affected investment activity. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
